Find the inverse of the following matrix: 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the inverse of the following matrix: 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that the given matrix is diagonal.

The inverse of a diagonal matrix can be found as follows: 

$$
{[\begin{aligned}{a}_{11} & 0 & ⋯ & 0 \\ 0 & {a}_{22} & ⋯ & 0 \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋱ & ⋮ \\ 0 & 0 & ⋯ & {a}_{nn}\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{a}_{11}} & 0 & ⋯ & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{{a}_{22}} & ⋯ & 0 \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋱ & ⋮ \\ 0 & 0 & ⋯ & \frac{1}{{a}_{nn}}\end{aligned}]
$$

In our case, we obtain

$$
{A}^{-1}={[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -\sqrt{3} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$
